header:
Date: 2026-06-02
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Head of ML, NexaHealth), James Park (CTO, NexaHealth), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Samir Patel (Security)
Recording: yes
transcript: [00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick check in - how we doing on the onboarding tasks from last week?

[00:12] Maya Lopez: Morning Liam, yeah overall good, we hit a snag with the VPC peering request - our infra team flagged some firewall rules that need adjustment, so that's blocking the test cluster access right now.
[00:28] Sofia Martinez: Got it. Aisha, do you have the peering request id? We can try to validate from our side too.
[00:35] Aisha Khan: Yeah the PR-457, I put it in the ticket but the security folks want explicit CIDR ranges instead of broad ranges - I can update that by EOD today.

[00:47] Liam Chen: Perfect, if you can update it we'll try to accept and then Sofia can attempt a quick smoke test. Also I emailed the service account keys but we should confirm key rotation policy with Samir.
[01:05] Samir Patel: Right, for production we need KMS + HSM notes, and audit logs retention - 1 year minimum is our baseline. Do you support customer-managed keys?

[01:18] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we support KMS integration and can use customer-managed keys in the private deploy path. For the hosted POC we can also show envelope encryption - I'll send the integration steps. There's a doc link in the deck I shared earlier.
[01:34] James Park: Quick question on performance - last run you mentioned 95th perc latency at 180ms on the dev config, is that still what we should expect?

[01:45] Sofia Martinez: It depends - that number was on A100-backed dedicated nodes with a batch size of 8 and prefix caching enabled. If you use smaller GPUs or hosted small instances you'll see higher latency. We can run identical benchmarks in your test VPC to compare.

[02:01] Maya Lopez: Okay, ideal for us would be a baseline of <200ms for single-request chat flows and throughput of ~200 reqs/min for our test dataset. We'll provide a representative prompt set by tomorrow.
[02:15] Liam Chen: Great - send the prompt set to the shared folder and we'll orchestrate the 1k-request run. Sofia, can you estimate how long the benchmark will take once infra is available?

[02:26] Sofia Martinez: The run itself is about 20-30 minutes for 1k requests, plus setup time - if peering is done today we can run tomorrow morning. Note: we'll instrument token-level traces, but that can be redacted for PHI before sharing results.
[02:45] Aisha Khan: About PHI, Samir wants to confirm data retention on logs - do you persist prompts on Redwood hosted?

[02:54] Liam Chen: For hosted we have configurable retention; by default we store short-term logs but for enterprise pilot we can turn off retention or send logs to your SIEM via syslog. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[03:06] Samir Patel: Also need SOC2 attestation copy and ISO details - last time I saw a token 'SOC' in the portal screenshot but need the report.
[03:15] Sofia Martinez: I'll attach SOC2 Type II and the ISO cert in the security folder. Expect a link in the follow-up email.
[03:25] James Park: There's also a question on model versioning - can you pin a model and roll forward in canary? We want deterministic outputs during the evaluation window.
[03:36] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we support pinned model versions and can run canary rollouts with traffic splits. For POC, we'll pin to the current stable v1.2 build and only change on sign-off.
[03:48] Maya Lopez: Good, and what about quantized variants? Our cost team asked about int8 options.

[03:55] Sofia Martinez: We do offer quantized profiles - Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization vs latency tradeoffs. For POC we can test a quantized profile in a separate run; results will show token throughput and output diffs.
[04:08] Liam Chen: Back to access - Aisha, once you update the PR with CIDRs we'll need the service account email so we can validate IAM roles. Can you paste that in the ticket?
[04:18] Aisha Khan: Yep, service account is nexah-poc-sa@corp.nexahealth.com - I'll add it now.
[04:25] Sofia Martinez: Thanks, I'll check IAM and confirm the minimal roles needed (compute.viewer, storage.objectViewer for artifacts, and logging.write to capture traces).
[04:40] James Park: On pricing - Liam, can you remind us of the committed-tier numbers for Dedicated vs hosted pilot? We're trying to figure monthly burn if we scale test traffic.

[04:52] Liam Chen: Sure. For pilot scale, hosted is pay-as-you-go - approx $0.015 per token for the model family we discussed; Dedicated reserved pools start at ~$8k/month for the starter bundle. I'll send exact breakdown in the SOW.
[05:06] Maya Lopez: That $8k - is that per 8xA100 or per cluster? We have to align with procurement.
[05:12] Liam Chen: It's for the entry reserved capacity package - I'll include per-GPU effective cost in the doc so procurement can compare.
[05:20] Aisha Khan: Another nit - our infra team needs the egress IPs for allowlisting. Can you provide those or a cached list?

[05:29] Sofia Martinez: For hosted endpoints we provide a range; for private deployments you control egress. I'll paste the hosted IP ranges in the email; for the VPC peering test there is no public egress.
[05:40] Samir Patel: On monitoring: do you emit traces to our Datadog or is it Redwood console only?
[05:47] Sofia Martinez: We can push metrics to Datadog via exporter, and provide token-level cost/latency breakdown in Redwood Console. We'll include sample dashboards for Datadog.
[05:58] James Park: Cool. Any blockers on the security documentation? We need the penetration test summary as well.
[06:05] Liam Chen: We have a pen-test summary available; Sofia will share the redacted version.
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: Yep, link will be in the security folder. Also I'll include the KMS/HSM integration note and the audit log retention options (S3 or SIEM push).
[06:25] Maya Lopez: Practical question - once the peering is accepted, what's the canonical test we run? Just the 1k prompt throughput or do we run session-based chat load?

[06:36] Sofia Martinez: We'll do both: 1k single-shot requests for per-request latency distribution, and a separate session-based run that simulates conversations at concurrency levels you expect. We'll provide the scripts we use so you can re-run.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: When you run tests will there be any PII redaction? We need to ensure no PHI leaves the VPC during runs.
[06:58] Sofia Martinez: For the VPC private run, data stays in your VPC. For hosted runs we can enable PII redaction hooks or mask before logs are stored. We'll show configuration options.

[07:10] Liam Chen: Quick timeline recap: Aisha updates PR today, Sofia shares VPC checklist by Wednesday, Liam sends pricing & SOW by Thursday, bench run once infra is ready, results by next Monday. Sound right?
[07:22] Maya Lopez: Yes that aligns. Also we'll upload the prompt set by EOD tomorrow so you can prep the scripts.
[07:30] James Park: One more item - can you validate that your runtime supports KV cache warmup? Our product uses a lot of repeated prefixes.

[07:39] Sofia Martinez: Yes, runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching; we can pre-warm cache during the benchmark. There was an earlier transcript typo where KV cash was written, lol - that was from the auto-transcribe.
[07:52] Aisha Khan: Haha, yes saw the 'K-V cash' in the doc - good to confirm.
[07:58] Liam Chen: Alright, any procurement paperwork we should expect from you? Maya or James?
[08:04] James Park: We'll likely need a short SOW and an NDA addendum for the PHI aspects. Procurement will review once we have the SOW numbers.
[08:12] Liam Chen: I'll include a pilot SOW template and the optional PHI addendum. Also adding the security docs and SOC2 link.
[08:20] Samir Patel: Please ensure the SOW includes data handling and breach notification timelines - 72 hours standard for us.
[08:27] Liam Chen: Noted, we'll add that clause.
[08:33] Sofia Martinez: Practical next step for me: I'll attempt to SSH into the test node after peering to validate role bindings, then run the smoke test and post the logs to the folder.
[08:44] Aisha Khan: Sounds good - I'll ping once PR updated and service account added.
[08:50] Liam Chen: Perfect. Anything else?
[08:54] Maya Lopez: No, that's it from me. Thanks all.

[08:57] Liam Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the links and action item list in an email. Chat notes: shared deck link: https://redwood.app/s/abc123 (security & VPC checklists), benchmark script: https://drive.nexah/example (placeholder).
[09:12] Sofia Martinez: I'll send the SOC2 and penetration summary; also attaching the VPC checklist and RBAC snippet.

[09:20] Liam Chen: Recap of next steps (quick): Liam - pricing + SOW by 6/4; Sofia - VPC checklist + KMS notes by 6/3; Aisha - update PR & add service account by 6/2 EOD; run bench once infra is live and share results by 6/7. Meeting close.
[09:40] Maya Lopez: Thanks everyone, bye.
[09:43] James Park: Bye.
